newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut praises end of U.S. travel ban on Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Beirut praises end of U.S. travel ban on Lebanon.

text.p: Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri praised the U.S. decision on Wednesday to end a ban on American citizens travelling to Lebanon, calling it a vote of confidence in the security situation in the country.

"I think this is something great and we are very happy," Hariri told Reuters in a telephone interview minutes after U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright announced she would not extend the travel ban in force since 1987.

The ban was imposed after the 1985 hijacking of a TWA airliner to Beirut during which a U.S. passenger was killed and amid a spate of kidnappings of foreigners -- mainly Americans -- by Moslem fundamentalists opposed to U.S. policy in the region.
"This is a vote of confidence in Lebanon, especially in the area of security," said Hariri.
The Lebanese prime minister said he had just finished a phone conversation with Albright, who was in Guam when she made the announcement. "She just talked to me to tell me the decision."

Lebanon had long campaigned for a lifting of the travel ban, which it said was no longer justified with the release of the last kidnap victims more than five years ago and the ending of the 15-year civil war in 1990.
